course_description:
To undertake practicum, students must meet all mandatory requirements as outlined here: Prepare for your Exercise and Sports Sciences placement and provider specific requirements.

HMST4314 is one of the capstone courses within the Exercise and Sport Sciences program. It provides students with the opportunity to engage in a minimum of 400 hours of work integrated learning in any of (but not limited to) the following settings.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate the skills and competencies required to work competently and confidently with low to moderate risk clients; and recognise the need for referral to other related professionals when appropriate. As described within the scope of practice by Exercise and Sport Science Australia (ESSA) for Exercise Science (400 hours minimum)
Demonstrate professional conduct that is sensitive to client diversity and equity and is consistent with the ESSA Code of Professional Conduct and Ethical Practice
Develop scientific rationale for professional decision making and service delivery, appropriate time management and ability to work collaboratively, and independently (as appropriate)

Demonstrate the ability to use research skills to critically evaluate specific areas of assessment, client centered interventions and/or education to determine whether research evidence indicates that current practice should be maintained or modified
Demonstrate effective written and oral communication skills relevant to the profession

assessment_details.title: Initial Logbook Submission
assessment_details.due_date: 5:00 pm on the Friday of Week 3 of placement.
assessment_details.task_description: To meet HMST4314 requirements during your placement, a logbook must be kept detailing all relevant practicum hours. A minimum of 400 hours of practicum is required across a range of sports science activities to demonstrate competency in assessment, analysis, programming, and delivery within the Accredited Sports Scientist (ASpS) scope of practice. Practicum hours must be completed across multiple sports science disciplines, with at least 120 hours involving direct service delivery to athletes or sport science service users. The remaining hours may include assessment or analysis activities that reflect the ASpS scope of practice. The initial logbook submission is used to check that your practicum hours are being recorded in line with logbook reporting requirements. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:

The purpose of this assessment is to support your development as a reflective practitioner, guide professional growth, and identify strengths and areas requiring further improvement during the remainder of your placement. assessment_details.due_date: 5:00 pm, 14 calendar days following placement completion date
assessment_details.task_description: At the end of your placement, your supervisor will conduct a Final Professional Attributes Assessment to evaluate your overall performance and readiness for professional practice. This assessment uses the same four-point scale applied throughout your placement. This final assessment provides an opportunity for you and your supervisor to review your performance, acknowledge strengths, identify any remaining areas for development, and confirm that you have met the minimum professional competency required for successful course completion. Unlike the Professional Attributes Intermediate Assessment, the Professional Attributes Final Assessment is summative and contributes to your overall course result. To pass the placement, you must meet or exceed expectations in all Standards. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Practicum Project
assessment_details.due_date: 5:00 pm, 14 calendar days following placement completion date
assessment_details.task_description: The Practicum Project provides an opportunity for you to demonstrate applied professional learning during placement by contributing an educational resource relevant to your practicum context. You are required to identify a practice-relevant need within your placement setting and develop one applied educational resource that is relevant to the discipline of Sports Science and appropriate to the context of your placement. You are expected to propose your project idea(s) to your practicum supervisor for discussion and approval. The final educational resource should be informed by your placement experience and developed by you, with consultation from your practicum supervisor, with the aim of supporting clients, athletes, staff, students, or service delivery at the practicum site.
